title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 186 (Agent’s authority may be expressed or implied)

content.overview: Section 186 provides that the authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.
content.glance: The authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.
content.study: The authority of an agent may be expressed or implied. Current-law framing: both express and implied forms of authority are recognised.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.

examples.title: Express or implied
examples.body: An agent’s authority may be given expressly or arise by implication under Section 186.

hypotheticals.question: Must an agent’s authority always be express?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 186 provides that the authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.

learningObjectives: State Section 186's rule that an agent's authority may be expressed or implied.
enhancement.definition: The authority of an agent may be expressed or implied.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Agency authority may be express or implied.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 186 provides that the authority of an agent may be expressed or implied. This establishes that both forms of authority are recognised in the law of agency.
examples: Authority may be given by words or arise from circumstances.
distinctions: Section 186 states the principle; Section 187 defines express and implied authority.
problemApplication: Identify whether authority is claimed as express or implied.
Conclude that both are permissible under Section 186.

shortAnswer: Conclude authority may be expressed or implied

keyTakeaways: An agent’s authority may be expressed or implied.
